content_voiceover: This is the International Prognostic Index, or I-P-I, and its revised version, R-I-P-I, for diffuse large B cell lymphoma. The original I-P-I scores five clinical factors, one point each: age over sixty, Ann Arbor stage three or four, E-C-O-G performance status two or higher, elevated serum L-D-H above the upper limit of normal, and more than one extranodal site of disease. Total points define four risk groups: low, zero to one point; low-intermediate, two points; high-intermediate, three points; and high, four to five points. But this original I-P-I was derived in the pre-rituximab era, so it was recalibrated after rituximab became standard, producing the revised I-P-I, which regroups the same five factors into just three categories: very good, zero points; good, one to two points; and poor, three to five points. The Kaplan-Meier curves show excellent discrimination: four year progression free survival is ninety four percent for very good, eighty percent for good, and fifty three percent for poor, with a similar pattern for four year overall survival, ninety four, seventy nine, and fifty five percent respectively.
keypoints: IPI: 1 point each for age >60, stage III/IV, ECOG ≥2, LDH >ULN, >1 extranodal site
IPI groups (pre-rituximab): low 0-1, low-intermediate 2, high-intermediate 3, high 4-5
R-IPI (rituximab era) regroups same factors: very good 0, good 1-2, poor 3-5
keypoint_voiceover: Know the five I-P-I factors cold: age over sixty, advanced stage, poor performance status, high L-D-H, and multiple extranodal sites, one point each. The original I-P-I splits into four risk groups, but since it predates rituximab, boards favor the revised I-P-I, which condenses those same factors into three groups, very good, good, and poor, with four year survival ranging from about ninety four percent down to around fifty five percent.
